description: Develop a solid understanding of fundamental text mining principles for extracting, transforming, and analyzing textual data, including regular expressions, text normalization, minimum edit distance, n-gram language models, smoothing, perplexity, entropy, vector semantics, TF-IDF, Word2Vec, and embedding evaluation.

Use machine learning and deep learning methods for text-mining applications, including Naive Bayes text classification and sentiment analysis, logistic and multinomial logistic regression, model evaluation, cross-validation, RNNs, LSTMs, attention, transformers, pretrained language models, masked language models, and fine-tuning.

Explore methods and algorithms for text classification and clustering tasks, including Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, k-means clustering, unsupervised text clustering, document similarity, and topic modeling.

Represent text data using bag-of-words, TF-IDF, and word embeddings, and evaluate their strengths and limitations through vector semantics, cosine similarity, pointwise mutual information, Word2Vec, embedding visualization, semantic properties, bias, and vector model evaluation.

Recognize and design real-world text-mining applications such as machine translation, question answering, and chatbots, including encoder-decoder translation, low-resource translation, translation evaluation, dialogue-state architecture, chatbot design, and dialogue-system evaluation.
